description: Manifest variant discovery (C3; contracts.md version discovery). A consumer GETs the catalog at /.well-known/aweb-app-versions.json, selects the highest manifest_version it supports, GETs that same-origin variant and verifies its digest, manifest_version and app.id. A catalog 404 alone permits the legacy /.well-known/aweb-app.json. Redirects are never followed and no failure falls back to another variant or to legacy. Consumers assert codes, never wording.
fetch_semantics: responses maps an origin-relative path to {status, body[, location]}. A path absent from responses answers 404. body is the exact UTF-8 response bytes; digests are sha256 over them. The consumer fetches only paths this contract names, at most 64 KiB for the catalog and the manifest bound for variants.

error_codes.catalog_unavailable: The catalog answered with a status other than 200 or 404.
error_codes.catalog_invalid: The catalog is not exactly one strict catalog_version 1 object with 1-8 variants of distinct positive manifest_version, a same-origin absolute path url without query, fragment or dot segments, and a sha256:<64 lowercase hex> digest.
error_codes.no_supported_variant: No catalog variant has a manifest_version the consumer supports.
error_codes.variant_unavailable: The selected variant answered with a status other than 200.
error_codes.variant_digest_mismatch: The selected variant's bytes do not hash to its catalog digest.
error_codes.variant_mismatch: The selected variant's manifest_version or app.id differs from its catalog entry or catalog app_id.
error_codes.legacy_unavailable: After a catalog 404, the legacy manifest answered with a status other than 200.
error_codes.v1_variant_incompatible: Publisher lint: the v1 variant is not an agent-safe, identically mapped subset of the v2 variant.

mutation_semantics: As in app-manifest-v2-v1.json: each lint side starts from base_manifests[base] and applies RFC 6901 JSON Pointer set/remove mutations; the result is serialized as JSON bytes.
lint_semantics: Publisher-side check that an app runs before serving both variants. The v1 variant must equal the v2 app object and events; every v1 tool must exist in v2 under the same name with identical method, path, params, input_schema, body, scopes, auth and mutation, and with agent in its v2 invocation_contexts; every v1 event_emitters (kid, did_key) must be a v2 app_keys entry with purpose app-event. The legacy path serves the v1 variant's exact bytes.
